article_title: KPMG partner fined for using artificial intelligence to cheat in AI training test
article_excerpt: A partner at KPMG has been fined for using AI to cheat during an internal AI training course. More than two dozen KPMG Australia staff have been caught using AI tools to cheat on internal exams since July. KPMG used its own AI detection tools to discover cheating. In 2021, KPMG Australia was fined A$615,000 for widespread improper answer-sharing. ACCA said it would require in-person exams because it was too difficult to stop AI cheating. KPMG and PwC have been mandating staff to use AI at work; KPMG partners will be assessed on AI tool usage in 2026 performance reviews.
question: Why is this a big deal specifically for accounting and audit firms (vs a normal company training scandal)?

article_title: Starmer to extend online safety rules to AI chatbots after Grok scandal
article_excerpt: UK plans to close a legal loophole so AI chatbot providers must comply with illegal content duties in the Online Safety Act or face consequences. Triggered by Grok scandal involving sexualised images. Government may accelerate restrictions on children's social media use. Ofcom said it lacked powers to act against Grok because chatbot-generated images/videos without web search were not in scope unless pornography. Penalties can be up to 10% of global revenue and courts can block services in the UK.
